name: Kintsugi
author: Erin Carter
description: Gold-repaired pottery: a solid lit ceramic glaze surface laced with a natural, irregular crackle network - wandering cracks that branch and meet at random angles the way real crazed glaze does. The cracks are filled with crisp metallic gold rendered as a lit rounded lacquer ridge, and the glaze between them carries its own shifting tone, soft sheen and iron speckle.

params.label: Crack scale
params.effect: Scale of the crackle network; low gives a few large bold cracks with big glaze fields between, high a finely crazed surface webbed with many cracks.

params.label: Seam width
params.effect: Width of the gold repair seams in CSS pixels - a fine lacquer line at the minimum, a broad molten channel of beaten gold at the maximum.

params.label: Fine cracks
params.effect: Amount of fine secondary craze threading between the main breaks; 0 leaves only the bold cracks, high webs the glaze with delicate hairline gold.

params.label: Glaze
params.effect: Depth and sheen of the ceramic glaze under the raking light; low is a flat matte body, high a deep lustrous raku glaze with a moving catchlight.

params.label: Light drift
params.effect: Speed the raking light drifts across the vessel, sweeping the glint along the gold ridges and the glaze sheen; 0 holds a fixed highlight.
